One liner: 51-year-old woman with depression and anxiety presenting after intentional acetaminophen overdose.

Chief complaint: "I took a bunch of Tylenol."

History of present illness: 51-year-old woman with major depressive disorder who reports ingesting approximately 40 tablets of acetaminophen 500 mg (~20 g) 6 hours ago after an argument with her partner. She called her sister, who brought her to the ED. She reports nausea but no vomiting, no abdominal pain. She denies co-ingestants, denies alcohol today. She expresses regret and agrees to stay for evaluation.

Past medical history: Major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, prior overdose 2019.

Medications: Sertraline 100 mg daily; Lorazepam 0.5 mg TID PRN anxiety; Acetaminophen 500 mg PRN (the overdose agent).

Social history: Lives with partner. Works part-time. No tobacco. Drinks wine socially.

Physical exam: VS: T 98.2 F, HR 88, BP 118/72, RR 14, SpO2 99% RA. Alert, tearful, cooperative. Abdomen soft, nontender. No asterixis.

Objective: Labs: Acetaminophen level 180 mcg/mL (H), AST 88 (H), ALT 74 (H), INR 1.1, Ethanol negative, Salicylates negative, UDS negative.

Assessment: 51-year-old woman with acute acetaminophen overdose, approximately 6 hours post-ingestion.

Plan:
1. Acetaminophen toxicity
- N-acetylcysteine IV per 21-hour protocol
- Repeat acetaminophen level, LFTs q6h
- Poison control consulted
2. Major depressive disorder with suicide attempt
- 1:1 observation, psychiatry consult
- Safety planning prior to any discharge consideration
3. Nausea
- Ondansetron PRN
